skill.name: create-mcp-skill
skill.description: Guides agents through creating skills that use MCP servers, including tool discovery, command testing, documentation templates, and optimized shell patterns.
skill.summary: Create MCP-powered skill documentation with discovery, testing, and reusable command patterns.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown code fences, inline examples, or documentation links rather than literal Ruby backtick execution, path traversal, or hardcoded network callbacks. Context review still found high-risk guidance: the skill encourages execution of user-supplied MCP server commands, unpinned package runners, and a broad filesystem server example. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, verify package sources, and ask for explicit confirmation before running any user-provided server command.

remediation.issue: Filesystem server example uses the home directory
remediation.suggestion: Use a narrow test directory in examples and warn users before granting an MCP server access to personal files.
Replace broad pkill patterns with exact PID cleanup, server-specific stop commands, or a clear manual confirmation step.
Generate least-privilege allowed-tools lists and add Bash or Write only when the target skill requires them.

semantic_findings.title: Unconstrained MCP Server Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks agents to run placeholder server commands and package runners such as bunx and npx. Without validation or version pinning, a user-provided server command can execute untrusted code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly instructs MCP CLI execution using target-controlled SERVER_COMMAND and latest package runners. This is a legitimate workflow, but it executes external binaries.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Home Directory Exposure in Example
semantic_findings.description: The filesystem server example points at the user home directory. That can give an MCP server broad access to personal files if copied into a real workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly invokes a filesystem MCP server with the home directory as its scope. The risk depends on user execution, but the guidance is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Process Termination Pattern
semantic_findings.description: The documented template repeatedly uses forceful process cleanup by pattern before running MCP shells. Broad pattern matching can kill unrelated processes or disrupt user work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple documented examples use forceful pattern-based cleanup. This can be safe for controlled test processes, but the template does not require exact process targeting.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Skill Permission Templates
semantic_findings.description: The current skill enables Bash, Read, Write, Edit, and Glob, and generated templates default to Bash, Read, and Write. This grants broad file and shell capabilities before target-specific need is established.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The frontmatter and generated templates explicitly grant broad tools. Some permissions are needed for this workflow, but least privilege is not enforced.

content.value_statement: Building a skill around an MCP server requires reliable discovery, testing, and documentation. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for MCP skill creation.
actual_capabilities: Lists MCP server tools and schemas using MCP CLI examples.
Provides a reusable SKILL.md template for MCP-based skills.
Shows shell-mode patterns for testing individual MCP tools.
Documents parameter formatting, timeout usage, and cleanup patterns.
Includes checklist guidance for performance, documentation, and troubleshooting.
limitations: Requires an installed MCP CLI and an available target server.
Uses shell command examples that need review before execution.
Does not verify the safety of third-party MCP packages.
Generated templates still require server-specific editing and testing.

use_cases.title: Create a new MCP skill
use_cases.description: Build a starter skill file after discovering a target MCP server and its tools.

use_cases.title: Standardize MCP skill documentation
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable structure for setup, quick starts, tool notes, and troubleshooting.

use_cases.title: Test MCP tool behavior
use_cases.description: Exercise MCP tools with controlled inputs before adding examples to a published skill.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic MCP skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a known MCP server.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new skill for my MCP server. Ask for the server command, discover available tools, and draft the initial SKILL.md.

prompt_templates.title: Document discovered tools
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn MCP tool discovery into user-facing documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the MCP tools I discovered. Summarize the useful tools, required parameters, optional parameters, and safe example tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize command examples
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve MCP examples for speed and reliability.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite my MCP skill examples to use shell mode, timeouts, clean exits, and concise troubleshooting notes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an MCP skill template
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before publishing a community skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this MCP skill draft for least-privilege tools, unsafe package execution, broad filesystem access, and unclear cleanup commands.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for a browser automation MCP server.
output: A skill folder plan with a clear SKILL.md outline.
A list of discovered browser tools and safe test tasks.
A quick start section with reviewed command patterns.

output_examples.input: Improve an existing MCP skill draft.
output: A revised structure for setup, quick starts, tool reference, and troubleshooting.
Notes about unsafe commands, broad permissions, and missing package pinning.
A checklist for testing examples before publication.

output_examples.input: Prepare documentation after MCP tool discovery.
output: Plain-language tool descriptions with parameter notes.
Warnings for optional parameters, timeouts, and server-specific quirks.
Practical next steps for completing the skill file.

best_practices: Pin third-party MCP package versions before copying command examples.
Test each MCP tool with harmless inputs before documenting workflows.
Keep generated skill permissions limited to the required tools.
anti_patterns: Using latest package versions in production skill examples.
Running user-supplied server commands without confirmation.
Copying broad process-kill patterns into unrelated skills.

faq.question: Does this skill run MCP servers automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command patterns, but execution still depends on the user's request and the agent's tool permissions.

faq.question: What tools does it require?
faq.answer: It expects an MCP CLI plus a target MCP server package or binary.

faq.question: Can it create a complete skill file?
faq.answer: Yes, it includes a starter SKILL.md structure and checklist, but server details still need editing.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted MCP packages?
faq.answer: No, untrusted packages should be pinned, reviewed, and tested in a sandbox first.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes, the workflow applies to Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when compatible tools are available.

faq.question: Can I customize command examples?
faq.answer: Yes, replace placeholders with reviewed server commands, safe inputs, and exact cleanup targets.
